source: reviewer_rubric_v3.py (rubric v3, RUBRIC_DELTAS B1 period = ICT 25-40 min)

universal.name: SLO Present & Non-Empty
universal.req: An SLO must exist with a clear action verb, ONE primary skill and a measurable outcome that matches the textbook page. A placeholder or empty field fails. No SNC or curriculum code is required (ICT LPs do not print one).
d: No SLO, or placeholder text (e.g. 'SLO will be added').
Present but only partially formed — missing action verb or outcome.
Action verb and outcome present, but a teacher would need to tweak it (too broad, or two skills in one).
One skill, matches the textbook page, and usable exactly as written — no editing needed.

universal.name: Hook Present & Non-Empty
universal.req: A Hook section must exist with at least 2 actionable teacher instructions — not a single vague line.
d: Hook missing, empty, or too thin to teach from (a line or two).
Some usable instructions, but missing a step a teacher would need.
At least 2 actionable teacher instructions present.
Fully formed, sequenced instructions an unfamiliar teacher could execute directly.

universal.name: Explanation Present & Non-Empty
universal.req: Explanation must have step-by-step instructions covering the core concept — not sparse filler.
d: Explanation missing, empty, or too thin to teach from (a line or two).
Some usable steps, but a clear gap (e.g. no worked example or no CFU).
Step-by-step instructions covering the core concept.
Comprehensive — definition, demonstration, examples, and CFUs all present.

universal.name: Practice Present & Non-Empty
universal.req: Practice must contain concrete student tasks, and all or most of them must match the SLO — one aligned task among off-target ones is not enough.
d: Practice missing, empty, or too thin to teach from (a line or two). Includes a Practice section with no actual task or question.
Tasks present, but only some match the SLO.
All or most practice tasks (guided and independent) match the SLO; at most one is off target.
Every practice task matches the SLO, with answer keys.

universal.name: Conclusion Present & Non-Empty
universal.req: Conclusion must include a specific closing activity (e.g. exit ticket, quiz) — not a vague directive.
d: Conclusion missing, empty, or too thin to teach from (a line or two).
Only a vague directive (e.g. 'Summarize the lesson').
A named closing activity (e.g. 'exit ticket: 3 questions'), but the questions are not written out.
The actual closing questions are written out with expected answers, and they test today's SLO.

universal.name: Single-Lesson Scope (One Class Period)
universal.req: LP must be ONE lesson for ONE class period (the region's period length (ICT: 25-40 min total; under 20 or over 50 = single-class failure)), targeting ONE SLO. BEFORE scoring, check for unit/chapter-plan red flags — if ANY is present this is a FUNDAMENTAL STRUCTURAL FAILURE (score 1) and you must NOT reward the quality of the sub-lessons inside it: a pacing table or weekly schedule; numbered 'Lesson 1, Lesson 2, …' headers; multiple SLOs (one per lesson) instead of one SLO; a chapter overview or full-chapter materials/assessment; a multi-lesson progress tracker; or a stated duration of multiple hours or 'X lessons × Y minutes'.
d: Unit/chapter plan packaged as one LP — ANY red flag present: pacing table or weekly schedule, numbered 'Lesson 1, 2, …' headers, multiple SLOs, chapter overview, multi-lesson progress tracker, or duration of multiple hours / 'X lessons × Y min'. FUNDAMENTAL STRUCTURAL FAILURE — do not reward the sub-lessons.
Single lesson but activity load is unrealistic for one 25-40 minute period (5+ distinct activities or multiple unrelated skills).
One lesson, one SLO, a realistic activity load for one class period (ICT: 25-40 min).
All of 3, plus times written for every section that add up to 25-40 minutes. Missing times caps this at 3.

universal.name: Measurable SLO
universal.req: The SLO outcome must be observable and measurable — teacher can check if students achieved it.
d: Cannot be measured; outcome not observable.
Somewhat measurable but lacks clear evidence of performance.
The SLO names something students do that the teacher can see (say, write, match).
The LP also says what counts as success (e.g. 'reads 5 of 6 words correctly', or an exit ticket with answers).

universal.name: Scaffolded Activities
universal.req: Activities must build on one another progressively toward SLO mastery — not be isolated or random.
d: Activities do not connect or build on one another.
Limited progression; partial link between steps.
Steps follow a sensible order toward the SLO.
Each step uses what the one before taught (e.g. I Do: the word -> We Do: the word in a sentence -> You Do: a new sentence), and no step could be skipped.

universal.name: Aligned with Textbook Content
universal.req: Lesson must use the actual textbook content (not just a page number). Judge the explanation and practice against the book; the hook and closing are not expected to come from it.
d: Lesson deviates from or ignores textbook material.
Uses textbook loosely without alignment to SLO.
The core explanation and practice use the textbook page (its text, items, pictures).
Also uses the book's own exercises in practice, with page numbers. The hook and closing do not have to come from the book.

universal.name: SLO–Assessment Alignment & Phase Coherence
universal.req: Check TWO things: (1) every assessment task (CFU, exit ticket) measures what the SLO requires, at the level of the SLO's action verb; (2) all phases target that same objective — no orphan activities.
d: Assessments have no visible link to SLO. OR one or more phases introduce content clearly outside the stated SLO.
Assessments loosely relate to SLO. OR most phases align but one activity feels disconnected from the objective.
The main checks (practice + exit ticket) measure the SLO, and no activity is off topic.
Every CFU and the exit ticket test the SLO's skill itself, not just its topic (e.g. SLO 'write a sentence using X' -> every check asks students to write one, not just to spot X).

universal.name: Opening Hook Relevant to SLO
universal.req: Hook must connect directly to the SLO — not a generic icebreaker. Only the link to the SLO is judged here; a missing or unrunnable hook is scored under 0B.
d: Hook unrelated to the SLO. (Whether a hook exists and can be run is scored under 0B, not here.)
Weakly connected to topic.
Engaging and related — connects to topic.
Strong, age-appropriate, directly linked to SLO; builds curiosity and context.

universal.name: Explicit Instructions & Evidence-Based Feedback Language
universal.req: Two things to check: (1) Instructions must say HOW to teach — specific steps, not 'explain X' or 'help students understand Y'. (2) Feedback instructions must be evidence-based and specific — not 'give feedback to students' but actual scripted response to common student errors (e.g. 'If student writes wrong denominator, say: Let's look at this together — what does the denominator represent?').
d: Instructions entirely generic ('Explain the concept', 'Give feedback'). No specific steps, no scripted feedback language.
Some specific instructions but feedback language is generic. Teacher would need to improvise how to respond to student errors.
Step-by-step instructions, and at least one scripted reply to a common student error.
A scripted reply at every point where students are likely to go wrong (I Do, We Do, You Do), so the teacher never has to improvise.

universal.name: Modelling / Demonstration with Think-Aloud
universal.req: I-Do must include step-by-step actions WITH reasoning aloud — not just 'explain X'. Look for: (1) each step has an action AND a 'Say:' prompt showing teacher's reasoning, (2) teacher verbalises WHY, not just WHAT. Generic instruction ('demonstrate the concept') scores 1–2.
d: No modelling. I-Do only says 'explain the concept' or 'teach X' — no steps, no reasoning shown.
Some steps present but no reasoning aloud. Teacher told WHAT to do but not HOW to verbalise cognitive process.
The teacher's reasoning is shown for most I Do steps.
Reasoning for every I Do step, plus the teacher names a common mistake and shows how to avoid it ('Some of you may think… but…').

universal.name: Smooth Transitions Across Steps
universal.req: Check logical flow and coherence between sections — NOT explicit bridging sentences. Do NOT suggest adding transition sentences.
d: Lesson feels disjointed or abrupt.
Some transitions but lack flow.
Sections come in a logical order.
Each section uses what the previous one produced (e.g. the We Do words come from the I Do list), so the teacher never has to invent a link. Extra transition sentences earn no credit.

universal.name: Practice Opportunities for Students
universal.req: Students must have opportunities to practice the skill — not just watch or listen. Look for tasks, questions, activities.
d: No practice opportunities.
Limited or unstructured practice.
Adequate practice supporting understanding.
Varied, well-sequenced practice (guided & independent) reinforcing SLO mastery.

universal.name: CFU Questions — Placed, Spaced & Open-Ended
universal.req: CFUs must: (1) appear AFTER concept is taught — not before, (2) be present after each phase (I Do, We Do, You Do) — 1-2 questions per phase, (3) be open-ended — not yes/no or single-word answers. Prior-knowledge questions in the Hook are NOT CFUs.
d: No CFUs anywhere in LP. OR all CFUs appear before the concept has been taught.
CFUs in only one phase, OR all CFU questions are closed (yes/no, fill-in-the-blank).
Open-ended CFUs in at least two of I Do / We Do / You Do.
Open-ended CFUs after all three phases, each with the expected answer and what to do if students get it wrong.

universal.name: Grade-Appropriate Strategies Aligned with SLO
universal.req: Teaching strategies must be suitable for the grade level and directly support the SLO — not generic or mismatched.
d: Strategies not suitable for grade/SLO.
Some strategies suitable but inconsistent.
Strategies mostly appropriate for grade/SLO.
Fully appropriate, effective, and tailored to SLO and learner level.

universal.name: Higher-Order Thinking (HOT) Opportunities
universal.req: At least one activity must require students to analyse, reason, apply, or evaluate — not just recall or copy.
d: All activities focus only on recall (copying, repeating, yes/no).
One higher-order question, but the rest is recall.
One full higher-order activity (students work on it, not just answer one question).
Two or more higher-order activities in different phases.

universal.name: Visual Aid Effectiveness
universal.req: Images/visuals must support instruction at the right moment — not decorative. If topic does not require visuals, score 3.
d: No images where visuals would clearly help, OR images present but irrelevant/decorative.
Images present but only partially useful — loosely related to topic.
Images present where helpful and prompts describe visuals that concretely support instruction.
Well-chosen images at the right instructional moment; prompts precise enough to serve as a direct teaching aid.

universal.name: Gradual Release — I Do → We Do → You Do
universal.req: All three phases must be identifiable: I Do (modelling with think-aloud), We Do (guided/shared practice with scaffolds — NOT just CFU questions), You Do (independent practice). We Do must include: (1) a collaborative or guided task, AND (2) scaffold support such as sentence stems, templates, or turn-and-talk protocol. A lesson going I Do → You Do with no We Do caps at Score 2.
d: No GRR structure — jumps from explanation to independent work, OR entirely teacher-led with no student practice.
GRR partially present — one phase missing or collapsed (e.g. We Do skipped or merged with You Do). OR We Do has a task but no scaffold support (no sentence stems, templates, or peer protocol).

All three phases present and distinct. We Do includes a guided task with at least one scaffold (sentence stem, template, or turn-and-talk instruction). You Do has clear independent instructions students can follow without teacher help.

GRR fully structured — I Do models with think-aloud, We Do has joint practice with scaffold templates and peer protocol, You Do is fully independent with clear instructions AND a self-checking mechanism (answer key, peer-check step, or checklist) so students know if they succeeded.

universal.name: Prior Knowledge Activation
universal.req: LP must include a deliberate activity or question that surfaces what students already know AND connects it to new content — not just 'Do you remember this topic?'
d: No attempt to activate prior knowledge. New content introduced without any connection to what students already know.
Prior knowledge referenced superficially — vague question with no follow-through connecting to new content.
Hook or Explanation opening includes a deliberate activity/question surfacing prior knowledge and connecting it to new content.
Prior knowledge activation is purposeful and diagnostic — teacher uses responses to calibrate lesson entry and maintains the connection through the Explanation.

universal.name: Active Retrieval (Warm-Up Recall)
universal.req: LP must open with a retrieval activity that: (1) links to a PRIOR SLO, (2) uses peer-mediated delivery (choral, pair-checking, or peer CFU) — NOT solo silent recall (solo silent = assessment only, not warm-up). Generic warm-ups without SLO link do not count.
d: No retrieval or warm-up activity at the start of the LP.
Warm-up not linked to a prior SLO, solo silent work, OR a teacher could not run it from the page.
LP opens with a peer-mediated recall activity (choral, pair-check, or peer CFU) clearly linked to a prior SLO.
Peer-mediated retrieval linked to a prior SLO, clear enough for a new teacher to run without guessing: who speaks, what students say, and the expected answers, plus a success check.

universal.name: Appropriately Timed Sections
universal.req: Time must be written per phase and total 25-40 minutes for one ICT class period. A total under 20 or over 50 minutes, or times clearly borrowed from multiple lessons, is a single-class failure — score 1 and also flag Criterion 0F. Check phase balance: I Do <=25% of total time, We Do >=30%, You Do >=30%. Example for a 35-min class: I Do <=9 min, We Do >=11 min, You Do >=11 min.
d: No time annotations anywhere; OR total under 20 or over 50 minutes; OR times clearly borrowed from multiple lessons (e.g. '8 lessons × 25–30 min', ~4 hours) — also flag Criterion 0F.
Times given for some but not all phases, with the total in a plausible single-class range (20–50 minutes).
Time written for all phases and total adds up to 25–40 minutes.
Time written for all phases, total is realistic, AND phase balance is correct: I Do ≤25%, We Do ≥30%, You Do ≥30%.

universal.name: Adequate Time for Practice & Explanation
universal.req: Practice (We Do + You Do combined) must receive at least 60% of lesson time. I Do must not dominate. Check that explanation time does not come at the expense of student practice time.
d: I Do takes more than 50% of lesson time — students have minimal practice.
Practice time too short for mastery (We Do + You Do under 50%), OR I Do under 5 minutes / with no worked example, which is too short to model anything.
Adequate time for both concept teaching and practice. We Do + You Do combined ≥60% of lesson time.
Excellent pacing — I Do is brief and focused, ample time for both guided and independent practice. No section feels rushed.

universal.name: Teacher Support Materials
universal.req: LP must provide answer keys, teacher notes, or background information — especially for less-experienced teachers.
d: No teacher notes, answer keys, or background provided.
Minimal guidance; not sufficient for a less-experienced teacher.
Answer keys, plus at least one note on a likely wrong answer and what to say back.
Answer keys for every task, and a wrong-answer note (what students may say, what to say back) for every task.

universal.name: Resource Requirements
universal.req: All required resources must be low-cost and available in Pakistani government schools (chalk, textbook, flashcards). No projector/internet required.
d: Depends on unavailable or expensive resources (projector, internet) with no alternatives.
Some resources impractical but substitutes partially implied.
Mostly low-cost or widely available resources (chalk, textbook, flashcards).
All resources explicitly low-cost, locally available, and feasible; alternatives offered where relevant.

universal.name: Teacher Flexibility / No Over-Scripting
universal.req: Instructions must be directive and clear without being rigidly word-for-word. Teacher must have natural space to respond to students. Directive verbs are good; complete scripting of every move is not.
d: So rigidly scripted word-for-word that the teacher has no room to respond to students or adapt.
Most instructions scripted; teacher feels constrained but could manage.
Directive and clear without being rigid — teacher knows what to do but has natural space to adapt.
Confident and guiding — structure provided without removing professional judgment.

universal.name: Suggestions for Struggling & Advanced Students
universal.req: LP must address BOTH struggling AND advanced students. Addressing only one group caps the score at 2.
d: No differentiation at all.
Only one group addressed (struggling OR advanced, not both).
Both groups addressed but strategies could be more specific.
Clear, actionable strategies for BOTH struggling AND advanced students.

universal.name: Named Differentiation Strategies with Instructions
universal.req: Score the instruction, not the label: a concrete, usable instruction for a group counts as a strategy even if it is not named (e.g. 'give struggling students the first word' is a scaffold).
d: No differentiation strategies named or described.
Strategy mentioned by concept only — no concrete tool or instruction.
One concrete, usable instruction for each of struggling and advanced learners.
Two or more concrete instructions for each group, each tied to a specific task.

universal.name: Instructional Language for Students
universal.req: Language used when addressing students must be clear, simple, and age-appropriate — not too complex or confusing.
d: Too complex or confusing for the target grade level.
Simplified but not consistent.
Clear and age-appropriate throughout.
Extremely simple, engaging, and culturally relevant for all learners.

universal.name: Instructional Language for Teachers
universal.req: Teacher-facing instructions must be clear, directive, and professional — actionable without being confusing or overly technical.
d: Unclear or overly technical.
Somewhat clear but inconsistent tone.
Clear, directive, and teacher-friendly.
Exceptionally clear, concise, and empowering for low-skill teachers.

universal.name: Active Student Participation
universal.req: Judged from the page: students must have a written-in output in each phase — talk prompts with expected answers, pair or choral turns, written work. Not just the teacher talking.
d: Entirely teacher-centred; students only listen or copy.
Students respond occasionally (chorus answers) but rarely produce independent output.
Most phases have students produce something (answers, pair talk, written work).
Every phase has a written-in student output (talk prompts with expected answers, pair or choral turns, a written task), so students say their thinking out loud, not just the answer.

universal.name: Peer Interaction Opportunities
universal.req: At least one structured peer interaction with clear instructions must be present — think-pair-share, pair work, group discussion, peer review.
d: No peer interaction; all activity between teacher and whole class.
One brief peer interaction but underdeveloped.
At least one structured peer interaction with clear instructions.
Multiple varied peer interactions (at least two different techniques) well integrated into lesson flow.

universal.name: Real-World Application
universal.req: At least one meaningful connection between lesson content and students' real lives must be present — not 'we use this in daily life' without an example.
d: No connection between lesson content and real-world use.
Real-world reference is superficial ('we use this in daily life') without example.
At least one meaningful, relevant real-world application that enhances understanding.
Real-world application is central and authentic — students apply knowledge to a genuine context from their lives.

universal.name: Exit Ticket — New Context, Success Criteria & Self-Prediction
universal.req: Every LP must end with an exit ticket that: (1) tests the SLO in a NEW context not seen in I-Do or We-Do, (2) includes instruction for teacher to read success criteria aloud before collecting, (3) includes a student self-prediction step (thumbs up/down or traffic light) before submitting.
d: No exit ticket or closing assessment.
Exit ticket present but repeats a classroom example. OR no success criteria. OR no self-prediction step.
Exit ticket uses a new context, tests the SLO. Teacher instructed to share success criteria before collecting.

Exit ticket in new context tests SLO at correct Bloom level. Success criteria read aloud. Students self-predict (thumbs/traffic light) before submitting. All three elements present and clearly instructed.

universal.name: Contextually Relevant Content
universal.req: Names, places, and scenarios must be relevant to Pakistani students' lives. No foreign currency, unrecognisable settings, or disconnected cultural references.
d: Uses foreign/irrelevant references (foreign currency, unrecognisable settings, disconnected names).
Mostly generic; some local references but incidental.
Names, places, scenarios clearly relevant to Pakistani students' lives.
Strongly rooted in local reality — familiar settings, culturally resonant stories, community-connected examples.

universal.name: Inclusive & Diverse Representation
universal.req: Examples must include both male and female names and diverse contexts. Deliberate — not accidental — inclusion of both genders.
d: No diversity in gender, background, or ability representation.
Limited diversity, largely incidental (e.g. only one gender in examples).
Deliberate effort to include diverse representation (both male and female names, different contexts).
Strong inclusive representation across gender, background, and ability — deliberately normalises diversity.

universal.name: Student Voice & Cultural Connection
universal.req: LP must explicitly invite students to connect content to their own experience, culture, or community — not just teacher-led examples.
d: Students never invited to connect content to their own lives or culture.
Surface-level prompt exists but does not invite genuine cultural or personal connection.
Students explicitly invited to connect content to their own experience, culture, or community.
Multiple opportunities for students to bring their own cultural knowledge and lived experience into the lesson.

universal.name: Language & Cultural Sensitivity
universal.req: Check for culturally inappropriate, insensitive, or exclusionary material. Language and examples must be respectful and appropriate for Pakistani classroom norms.
d: Contains culturally inappropriate, insensitive, or exclusionary material.
No overtly inappropriate content but may inadvertently exclude or stereotype.
Language and examples are culturally respectful and appropriate.
Respectful throughout, and no student group is marginalised or stereotyped (representing Pakistan's diversity is scored under 6B, not here).

universal.name: Internal Consistency & Plausible Textbook References
universal.req: Check for: (1) internal contradictions, (2) textbook references that seem fabricated (random page numbers, vague exercise names), (3) inconsistencies between sections.
d: Multiple internal contradictions, OR textbook references appear clearly fabricated.
Minor inconsistencies that could cause confusion, OR one suspicious reference.
Internally consistent; any textbook references are plausible and specific.
Fully coherent; all components reinforce one another; textbook references are detailed, specific, and consistent with subject/grade.

universal.name: Academic Content Accuracy
universal.req: Check for factual errors: incorrect maths steps, wrong scientific facts, grammatically wrong model sentences. Must be accurate and appropriate for grade level.
d: Factual errors (incorrect maths steps, wrong scientific facts, grammatically wrong sentences) that would mislead students.
Mostly accurate but minor errors or oversimplifications could create misconceptions.
Accurate and appropriate for grade level.
Fully accurate, age-appropriate, demonstrates clear subject knowledge — correct terminology and precise explanations.

universal.name: Bias and Balance
universal.req: Check for one-sided claims, harmful generalisations, missing important context, or negative stereotypes. Opinions/values must be framed as such.
d: Materially biased — one-sided claims, harmful generalisations, negative stereotypes, or missing important context.
Leans toward a particular viewpoint without acknowledgment, or minor stereotyping.
Balanced and fair — does not mislead or discriminate.
Explicitly balanced and objective; opinions/values clearly framed as such; multiple perspectives respected.

ENGLISH.name: Prioritised Skill Focus
ENGLISH.req: Lesson must target ONE primary skill from the English-7 taxonomy (pre_reading / phonics / reading_comprehension / vocabulary_grammar / writing / oral_communication / revision). Not spread across many.
d: Lesson tries to cover many skills with no primary focus.
One skill is dominant but others are still unnecessarily mixed in.
Lesson clearly targets one primary English-7 skill.
Primary skill explicitly named (English-7 key), all activities serve that skill.

ENGLISH.name: Named Teaching Strategies
ENGLISH.req: Must use specific, recognised English teaching strategies by name — e.g. phonics, shared reading, guided reading, think-aloud. Generic 'teaching' does not count.
d: No specific English strategy named; generic instructions only.
Strategy mentioned by name but not explained or incorrectly used.
At least one recognised English strategy used correctly.
Multiple named, recognised strategies used appropriately and in correct sequence for the skill focus.

ENGLISH.name: Evidence of Textbook Material Usage
ENGLISH.req: Textbook passages, vocabulary, or activities must be actively used — not just referenced by page number.
d: Textbook not used at all; entirely teacher-created content.
Textbook referenced by page number only without actually using content.
Textbook passages, vocabulary, or activities are actively used in the lesson.
Textbook content is central; teacher builds directly on textbook material with enrichment activities.

ENGLISH.name: Explicit Decoding Instruction (decoding/phonics lessons)
ENGLISH.req: The target grapheme-phoneme / letter-sound unit is TAUGHT explicitly: sound -> symbol -> blending sequence. Urdu: aadhi-ashkaal (آدھی اشکال) join/break shown for the target letters. Only applies to decoding/phonics-type lessons.
d: Decoding assumed, not taught (jumps straight to reading words).
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
Explicit sound->symbol->blend teaching sequence present for the target unit.
Explicit sound->symbol->blend teaching sequence present for the target unit. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

ENGLISH.name: Encoding Production (dictation/imla)
ENGLISH.req: Students WRITE the taught pattern — dictation/imla (املا) with a mark scheme (Urdu: connected-form-correct), not recognition only. Applies to decoding + writing lessons.
d: No student writing of the taught pattern (recognition only).
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
A scripted dictation/imla element with a mark scheme is present.
A scripted dictation/imla element with a mark scheme is present. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

ENGLISH.name: Decodable / Controlled Practice Text (phonics-stage reading)
ENGLISH.req: Reading-practice material is decodable with patterns already taught — not memorize-the-passage. Applies to phonics-stage reading-practice lessons.
d: Practice text requires untaught patterns (guessing/memorizing).
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
Practice text is controlled to taught patterns.
Practice text is controlled to taught patterns. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

ENGLISH.name: Fluency Drill (fluency lessons)
ENGLISH.req: A timed or repeated-reading element (buland-khwani drill) with a clear fluency criterion. Applies to fluency-type lessons.
d: No fluency element in a fluency lesson.
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
A repeated/timed reading drill with a stated criterion is present.
A repeated/timed reading drill with a stated criterion is present. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

ENGLISH.name: Communicative Beat (meaningful interaction)
ENGLISH.req: The lesson contains at least one moment where a child produces the target language TO ANOTHER PERSON who has a reason to hear it, and hears a response - with the exact words scripted for BOTH children (not 'children practise in pairs'). Applies to every language lesson type; the shape follows the type (phonics = partner sound-check, writing = partner dictation, reading = a listener with a job). Set notAssessable only for a pure motor pre_writing period.
d: No child-to-child production anywhere, or 'pair work' named but not scripted.
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
A scripted two-turn exchange with both children's words given, 2-5 minutes.
A scripted two-turn exchange with both children's words given, 2-5 minutes. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

ENGLISH.name: Information Gap or an honest declaration
ENGLISH.req: The productive activity's outcome cannot be reached without the exchange - one child holds what the other needs - OR the lesson honestly declares itself controlled practice ('none - controlled practice'). A declared 'none' is NOT a failure. What fails is display talk presented as communication: both children already hold the answer, or child A's script contains the answer B is meant to supply.
d: Display talk presented as communication (both children hold the answer; or A's script gives away B's answer).
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
A real gap with a checkable non-linguistic outcome, or an honest 'controlled practice' declaration.
A real gap with a checkable non-linguistic outcome, or an honest 'controlled practice' declaration. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

ENGLISH.name: Runnable by a non-native teacher (scripted classroom language + repair)
ENGLISH.req: The teacher's own language for setting up, running and stopping the interaction is given verbatim (or the course's own named routine/hand signs are cited), AND a fixed repair phrase is supplied for a stuck child. A teacher at A1-B1 cannot improvise an activity she has only been told the name of.
d: The activity is named but the teacher's words are not given.
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
Set-up / run / stop language present verbatim, plus a repair line for the child.
Set-up / run / stop language present verbatim, plus a repair line for the child. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

ENGLISH.name: Sayability + declared function
ENGLISH.req: Every word and frame the children are asked to say is already taught - the function is on this grade's list from the curriculum's own functions inventory, the words on the approved sources - and the lesson declares the child-facing function (can-do) it serves. An exchange built from untaught language is what produces L1 switching.
d: Children asked to produce untaught language, or no function declared.
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
All language taught, and the can-do function stated.
All language taught, and the can-do function stated. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

URDU.name: Prioritised Urdu Skill Focus
URDU.req: Lesson must target ONE primary skill from the Urdu-7 taxonomy (alfaaz_maani / buland_khwani / arkaan_saazi / qawaid / tafheem / takhleeqi_likhai / duhrai). There is deliberately NO standalone oral skill (speaking folds into buland_khwani, listening into tafheem) — that fold is NOT a violation.
d: Lesson covers multiple Urdu skills with no clear primary focus.
One skill attempted but others mixed in unnecessarily.
Lesson clearly targets one primary Urdu skill.
Primary skill explicitly named, all activities serve that skill, clear progression.

URDU.name: Named Urdu-Specific Teaching Strategies
URDU.req: Must use recognised Urdu pedagogical strategies by name — e.g. ہجے, خوش خطی, کہانی سنانا, قواعد. Generic instructions do not count.
d: No Urdu-specific strategy named; generic instructions only.
Strategy mentioned but not explained or incorrectly used.
At least one recognised Urdu strategy used correctly.
Multiple named Urdu strategies used appropriately and in correct pedagogical sequence.

URDU.name: Evidence of Textbook Material Usage
URDU.req: Urdu textbook poems, passages, or exercises must be actively used in the lesson — not just referenced by title or page.
d: Urdu textbook not used; entirely teacher-created content.
Textbook referenced by title/page only without using actual content.
Urdu textbook poems, passages, or exercises actively used in the lesson.
Textbook content is central; teacher builds directly from text with enrichment activities.

URDU.name: Multiple Strategy Variations & Alternatives
URDU.req: More than one teaching approach or strategy variant must be offered — giving teachers flexibility.
d: Only one approach used throughout with no alternatives.
Slight variation mentioned but not developed.
More than one teaching approach or strategy variant offered.
Multiple varied approaches with clear instructions for each; teacher has genuine flexibility.

URDU.name: Explicit Decoding Instruction (decoding/phonics lessons)
URDU.req: The target grapheme-phoneme / letter-sound unit is TAUGHT explicitly: sound -> symbol -> blending sequence. Urdu: aadhi-ashkaal (آدھی اشکال) join/break shown for the target letters. Only applies to decoding/phonics-type lessons.
d: Decoding assumed, not taught (jumps straight to reading words).
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
Explicit sound->symbol->blend teaching sequence present for the target unit.
Explicit sound->symbol->blend teaching sequence present for the target unit. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

URDU.name: Encoding Production (dictation/imla)
URDU.req: Students WRITE the taught pattern — dictation/imla (املا) with a mark scheme (Urdu: connected-form-correct), not recognition only. Applies to decoding + writing lessons.
d: No student writing of the taught pattern (recognition only).
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
A scripted dictation/imla element with a mark scheme is present.
A scripted dictation/imla element with a mark scheme is present. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

URDU.name: Decodable / Controlled Practice Text (phonics-stage reading)
URDU.req: Reading-practice material is decodable with patterns already taught — not memorize-the-passage. Applies to phonics-stage reading-practice lessons.
d: Practice text requires untaught patterns (guessing/memorizing).
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
Practice text is controlled to taught patterns.
Practice text is controlled to taught patterns. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

URDU.name: Fluency Drill (fluency lessons)
URDU.req: A timed or repeated-reading element (buland-khwani drill) with a clear fluency criterion. Applies to fluency-type lessons.
d: No fluency element in a fluency lesson.
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
A repeated/timed reading drill with a stated criterion is present.
A repeated/timed reading drill with a stated criterion is present. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

URDU.name: Communicative Beat (meaningful interaction)
URDU.req: The lesson contains at least one moment where a child produces the target language TO ANOTHER PERSON who has a reason to hear it, and hears a response - with the exact words scripted for BOTH children (not 'children practise in pairs'). Applies to every language lesson type; the shape follows the type (phonics = partner sound-check, writing = partner dictation, reading = a listener with a job). Set notAssessable only for a pure motor pre_writing period.
d: No child-to-child production anywhere, or 'pair work' named but not scripted.
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
A scripted two-turn exchange with both children's words given, 2-5 minutes.
A scripted two-turn exchange with both children's words given, 2-5 minutes. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

URDU.name: Information Gap or an honest declaration
URDU.req: The productive activity's outcome cannot be reached without the exchange - one child holds what the other needs - OR the lesson honestly declares itself controlled practice ('none - controlled practice'). A declared 'none' is NOT a failure. What fails is display talk presented as communication: both children already hold the answer, or child A's script contains the answer B is meant to supply.
d: Display talk presented as communication (both children hold the answer; or A's script gives away B's answer).
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
A real gap with a checkable non-linguistic outcome, or an honest 'controlled practice' declaration.
A real gap with a checkable non-linguistic outcome, or an honest 'controlled practice' declaration. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

URDU.name: Runnable by a non-native teacher (scripted classroom language + repair)
URDU.req: The teacher's own language for setting up, running and stopping the interaction is given verbatim (or the course's own named routine/hand signs are cited), AND a fixed repair phrase is supplied for a stuck child. A teacher at A1-B1 cannot improvise an activity she has only been told the name of.
d: The activity is named but the teacher's words are not given.
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
Set-up / run / stop language present verbatim, plus a repair line for the child.
Set-up / run / stop language present verbatim, plus a repair line for the child. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

URDU.name: Sayability + declared function
URDU.req: Every word and frame the children are asked to say is already taught - the function is on this grade's list from the curriculum's own functions inventory, the words on the approved sources - and the lesson declares the child-facing function (can-do) it serves. An exchange built from untaught language is what produces L1 switching.
d: Children asked to produce untaught language, or no function declared.
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
All language taught, and the can-do function stated.
All language taught, and the can-do function stated. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

MATHS.name: Conceptual Knowledge
MATHS.req: Students must understand WHY behind procedures — not just mechanical steps. Look for explanation of the concept, not just the method.
d: Lesson only teaches procedures/steps; no explanation of why.
Some conceptual explanation but mostly procedural focus.
Students understand the 'why' behind procedures through explanation and examples.
Conceptual understanding built through concrete examples, connections to prior knowledge, and multiple representations.

MATHS.name: Computational Skills — Step-by-Step Guidance
MATHS.req: Teacher must show full worked examples step by step. Every calculation step must be visible — not just the answer.
d: No step-by-step modelling; teacher tells answer without showing working.
Some steps shown but incomplete or unclear.
Clear step-by-step teacher modelling of calculations with worked examples.
Full worked examples with each step explained, common errors addressed, and multiple practice examples provided.

MATHS.name: Real-World Application
MATHS.req: Problems must be set in meaningful, locally relevant contexts (e.g. shopping, measurement, sharing) — not abstract numbers.
d: Problems use abstract numbers with no context.
Context mentioned but forced or unrealistic.
Problems set in locally relevant contexts (shopping, measurement, sharing).
Real-world application is central; students solve problems from their own lives with meaningful context throughout the lesson.

MATHS.name: Mathematical Language & Dialogue
MATHS.req: Correct mathematical vocabulary must be used AND students must be asked to use it — e.g. 'sum', 'product', 'denominator', 'numerator'.
d: No mathematical vocabulary used or taught.
Some terms used but not explicitly taught or practiced.
Correct mathematical vocabulary used and students asked to use it.
Mathematical language systematically introduced, defined, practiced, and reinforced throughout the lesson.

MATHS.name: Number-Sense Warm-Up
MATHS.req: The opening includes number-sense work (subitizing / counting / composing-decomposing), not only fact recall.
d: No number-sense element in the warm-up.
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
A short number-sense warm-up activity is scripted.
A short number-sense warm-up activity is scripted. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

MATHS.name: CPA-Phase Fidelity
MATHS.req: The lesson enacts its assigned CPA phase (concrete = real objects/actions; pictorial = images/diagrams; abstract = symbols only after earlier phases). A NEW concept never starts abstract.
d: Phase mismatch (e.g. a 'concrete' lesson with no objects/actions; new concept starts abstract).
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
Activities visibly match the assigned CPA phase.
Activities visibly match the assigned CPA phase. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

MATHS.name: Fact-Fluency + Mastery Check
MATHS.req: A short fluency element AND an explicit mastery criterion ('students can X before moving on').
d: Neither fluency practice nor a mastery criterion present.
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
Both a brief fluency element and a stated mastery criterion are present.
Both a brief fluency element and a stated mastery criterion are present. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

SCIENCE.name: Scientific Concept Clarity
SCIENCE.req: Core scientific concept must be accurately explained in simple, age-appropriate language — not overly technical or vague.
d: Core concept is missing, incorrect, or confusing for the grade level.
Concept is present but too vague, overly complex, or partially inaccurate.
Core concept accurately explained in simple, age-appropriate language.
Concept is clear, accurate, age-appropriate, and supported with examples, visuals, or simple demonstrations.

SCIENCE.name: Hands-On / Observation-Based Learning
SCIENCE.req: Must include a practical activity, experiment, demonstration, or observation — not only text or lecture. For concepts where hands-on is not feasible, a structured model or guided visual qualifies if students produce observable output.
d: Lesson relies only on teacher explanation, textbook reading, or copying; no activity.
Activity mentioned but unclear, impractical, or not directly linked to the concept.
Includes a practical activity, experiment, demonstration, or observation linked to the SLO.
Well-sequenced hands-on/observation task using simple/local materials, with clear teacher instructions and expected student responses.

SCIENCE.name: Real-Life Connections
SCIENCE.req: Concept must be connected to students' environment or daily experience — household materials, school, weather, local plants/animals.
d: No connection to students' daily life, environment, or local context.
Real-life connection is generic or superficial without specific examples.
Concept connected to students' environment, household materials, school, or local surroundings.
Real-life connection runs through the whole lesson as the main vehicle for explanation — not just introduced at start but used repeatedly.

SCIENCE.name: Scientific Inquiry & CFUs
SCIENCE.req: Students must be prompted to observe, predict, ask questions, or draw conclusions. CFUs must be concept-specific — not generic. At minimum 2–3 inquiry moments.
d: No inquiry, prediction, observation question, conclusion, or concept-specific CFU.
Some questions included but mostly recall-based or not linked to the science concept.
Students asked to observe, predict, answer concept-specific CFUs, or draw simple conclusions.
Inquiry integrated throughout: students ask/answer questions, make predictions, observe evidence, explain reasoning. Minimum 2–3 inquiry moments.

SCIENCE.name: Investigate-Before-Explain (POE ordering)
SCIENCE.req: Within the lesson's 5E position, observation/prediction precedes the concept statement (predict-observe-explain); a concept_build lesson references the prior investigation.
d: Concept stated first; investigation absent or decorative.
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
Prediction/observation genuinely precedes and feeds the explanation.
Prediction/observation genuinely precedes and feeds the explanation. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

SCIENCE.name: Bilingual Concept Glossary
SCIENCE.req: New science terms carry an English term-of-record + Urdu gloss (translanguaging free at hook; English pinned at concept/assess).
d: New terms introduced in one language only, no gloss.
Attempted but superficial or wrong.
Each new term has the EN term + Urdu gloss at first use.
Each new term has the EN term + Urdu gloss at first use. Exemplary: explicit, scripted, immediately teachable.

GK.name: Concept & Vocabulary Clarity
GK.req: GK concept must be explained clearly in simple Urdu. New vocabulary must be introduced, written, pronounced, and used in context.
d: GK concept missing, unclear, or too difficult; key vocabulary not introduced.
Concept explained briefly but vocabulary support is weak or inconsistent.
Core concept explained clearly in simple Urdu; key words introduced and used in context.
Concept very clear and age-appropriate; new words written, pronounced, repeated, explained, and used in examples for low-vocabulary learners.

GK.name: Observation, Exploration & Inquiry
GK.req: Lesson must include an age-appropriate activity where students observe, explore, compare, or ask questions — not just reading or lecture.
d: Lesson relies only on reading, lecture, or memorization; no exploration.
Activity exists but mostly passive, unclear, or weakly linked to concept.
Includes an age-appropriate activity where students observe, explore, compare, predict, or ask questions.
Exploration strongly embedded; students actively observe, compare, discuss, make predictions. Multiple inquiry moments throughout.

GK.name: Real-Life & Local Context Connection
GK.req: Concept must be connected to students' daily life, classroom, home, community, Pakistani culture, or local examples.
d: Content generic, foreign, or disconnected from students' lives.
Some local examples present but incidental or not clearly connected to concept.
Concept connected to students' daily life, classroom, home, community, or local examples.
Local context woven throughout as main anchor for understanding — not just mentioned but repeatedly used. Examples culturally appropriate and familiar.

GK.name: Integrated GK Theme Handling
GK.req: Lesson must handle GK topic according to its nature: science topics need observation; social/citizenship topics need behaviour/values; environment topics need local examples.
d: Lesson treats all GK topics the same way with no attention to topic nature.
Topic type somewhat addressed but inconsistently.
Lesson handles the GK topic appropriately according to its theme (science, environment, social, values, citizenship).
Topic handling is strong and purposeful: science builds through observation; citizenship builds behaviour/responsibility; environment uses local surroundings.

SST.name: Concept & Vocabulary Clarity
SST.req: SSt concept must be explained clearly in simple Urdu. New terms (history, geography, citizenship) must be introduced and used in context.
d: SSt concept missing, unclear, or too difficult; key terms not explained.
Concept present but vague; vocabulary translated or explained only partially.
Concept explained clearly in simple Urdu; key SSt terms introduced and used in context.
Concept very clear and age-appropriate; new terms broken down, translated, repeated, written, and used in understandable examples.

SST.name: Use of SSt Tools & Organizers
SST.req: For topics requiring tools (maps for geography, timelines for history, concept maps for civic topics), a relevant tool must be used. Not all SSt lessons require tools — assess only when topic naturally calls for one.
d: No relevant SSt tool used where one would clearly support understanding.
Tool mentioned or used superficially (e.g. map shown without clear teaching purpose).
Lesson uses a relevant tool (map, timeline, chart, mind map, or board drawing) to explain the topic.
Tool use purposeful and well integrated; students actively use or interpret maps, timelines, charts, or organizers.

SST.name: Local Context, Storytelling & Real-Life Relevance
SST.req: Lesson must use storytelling, local examples, Pakistani/Islamic cultural context, or real-life scenarios. Ideally students make personal connections.
d: Lesson dry, memorization-based, or disconnected from students' community and daily life.
Some example or story included but weakly connected to main concept.
Teacher-led relevance: lesson uses storytelling, local examples, Pakistani context, or real-life scenarios to explain topic.
Student-led relevance: students actively make personal connections to their own lives, community, responsibilities, or experiences.

SST.name: Historical, Geographical or Civic Thinking
SST.req: Students must be prompted to think — sequence events, compare places, identify cause/effect, discuss responsibilities. Not just memorize facts.
d: Lesson focuses only on memorizing facts, names, dates, or definitions.
One thinking task included but mostly recall-based.
Students prompted to sequence events, compare places, identify cause/effect, or explain why topic matters.
Thinking woven throughout; students reason, compare, explain causes/effects, discuss civic responsibilities, and connect topic to broader social understanding.

ISLAMIAT.name: Accuracy of Islamic Concepts & Teachings
ISLAMIAT.req: Islamic concepts, beliefs, Quran/Hadith references, or religious practices must be accurate, respectful, and age-appropriate. Any inaccuracy must be flagged.
d: Islamic concept, value, or religious explanation is incorrect, careless, or misleading.
Mostly correct but vague, incomplete, or not clearly age-appropriate.
Islamic concept or teaching is accurate, respectful, and age-appropriate.
Accurate, respectful, clear, age-appropriate, and strengthens understanding through suitable examples or teacher guidance.

ISLAMIAT.name: Values-to-Life Connection
ISLAMIAT.req: Lesson must connect Islamic teaching to students' daily actions, manners, responsibilities, or moral choices — not just memorization.
d: Lesson focuses only on memorization; no connection to behaviour or daily life.
Life connection present but generic ('we should be good Muslims') without concrete examples.
Lesson connects Islamic teaching to students' daily actions, manners, responsibilities, or social behaviour.
Values-to-life connection meaningful and practical; students identify how to apply teaching in home, school, community, or social situations.

ISLAMIAT.name: Key Vocabulary & Recitation Support
ISLAMIAT.req: Important Islamic terms, Arabic/Urdu words, duas, or ayat must be written, pronounced, repeated, and practiced clearly.
d: Important Islamic terms, duas, or ayat not supported or practiced.
Vocabulary or recitation mentioned but pronunciation, repetition, or practice is limited.
Key terms or recitation items are written, pronounced, repeated, and practiced clearly.
Vocabulary and recitation support is strong: teacher models pronunciation, students repeat, meanings explained simply, practice structured for accuracy.

ISLAMIAT.name: Respectful & Culturally Appropriate Framing
ISLAMIAT.req: All examples, activities, and teacher language must be respectful, aligned with Islamic values, and appropriate for Pakistani classroom norms.
d: Lesson includes inappropriate comparisons, careless wording, or content conflicting with Islamic values/Pakistani norms.
No major issue, but some wording or examples feel weak, insensitive, or not carefully framed.
Examples, teacher language, and activities are respectful, culturally appropriate, and aligned with Islamic values.
Framing thoughtful and sensitive throughout; promotes respect, good manners, and inclusion without stereotyping.
